arxiv-1609-09840.title: Regular and almost universal hashing: an efficient implementation
arxiv-1609-09840.creator: D. Ivanchykhin, S. Ignatchenko, D. Lemire
arxiv-1609-09840.description: Abstract Random hashing can provide guarantees regarding the performance of data structures such as hash tables—even in an adversarial setting. Many existing families of hash functions are universal: given two data objects, the probability that they have the same hash value is low given that we pick hash functions at random.

arxiv-2112-04690.title: Polarization-dependent magnetic properties of periodically driven α \alpha -RuCl 3
arxiv-2112-04690.creator: Naoya Arakawa, Kenji Yonemitsu
arxiv-2112-04690.description: Abstract We study magnetic properties of a periodically driven Mott insulator with strong spin-orbit coupling and show some properties characteristic of linearly polarized light. We consider a t 2 ​ g t_{2g} -orbital Hubbard model driven by circularly or linearly polarized light with strong spin-orbit coupling and derive its effective Hamiltonian in the strong-interaction limit for a high-frequency case.

arxiv-2206-10673.title: Natural Backdoor Datasets
arxiv-2206-10673.creator: Emily WengerUniversity of Chicago, Roma BhattacharjeePrinceton UniversityArjun Nitin BhagojiUniversity of ChicagoJosephine PassanantiUniversity of ChicagoEmilio AndereUniversity of ChicagoHaitao ZhengUniversity of ChicagoBen Y. ZhaoUniversity of Chicago
arxiv-2206-10673.description: Abstract Extensive literature on backdoor poison attacks has studied attacks and defenses for backdoors using “digital trigger patterns.” In contrast, “physical backdoors” use physical objects as triggers, have only recently been identified, and are qualitatively different enough to resist all defenses targeting digital trigger backdoors.

arxiv-2301-02683.title: Classifying topological neural network quantum states via diffusion maps
arxiv-2301-02683.creator: Yanting Teng, Subir Sachdev, Mathias S. Scheurer
arxiv-2301-02683.description: Abstract We discuss and demonstrate an unsupervised machine-learning procedure to detect topological order in quantum many-body systems. Using a restricted Boltzmann machine to define a variational ansatz for the low-energy spectrum, we sample wave functions with probability decaying exponentially with their variational energy; this defines our training dataset that we use as input to a diffusion map scheme.

arxiv-2402-07741.title: Monodromy of elliptic logarithms: some topological methods and effective results
arxiv-2402-07741.creator: Francesco Tropeano
arxiv-2402-07741.description: Abstract We present some effective approaches in studying the relative monodromy group of elliptic logarithms with respect to periods of elliptic schemes. We provide explicit ways of constructing explicit loops which leave periods unchanged but along which logarithms have non-trivial variations. We also get some topological methods and effective results which allow to manage the ramification locus of sections.

arxiv-2404-17698.title: “Actually I Can Count My Blessings”: User-Centered Design of an Application to Promote Gratitude Among Young Adults
arxiv-2404-17698.creator: Ananya Bhattacharjee, Zichen Gong, Bingcheng Wang, Timothy James Luckcock, Emma Watson, Elena Allica Abellan, Leslie Gutman, Anne Hsu, Joseph Jay Williams
arxiv-2404-17698.description: Abstract . Regular practice of gratitude has the potential to enhance psychological wellbeing and foster stronger social connections among young adults. However, there is a lack of research investigating user needs and expectations regarding gratitude-promoting applications. To address this gap, we employed a user-centered design approach to develop a mobile application that facilitates gratitude practice.

arxiv-2501-10596.title: Evaluating Amazon Effects and the Limited Impact of COVID-19 With Purchases Crowdsourced from US Consumers
arxiv-2501-10596.creator: Alex Berke
arxiv-2501-10596.description: Abstract Abstract We leverage a recently published dataset of Amazon purchase histories, crowdsourced from thousands of US consumers, to study how online purchasing behaviors have changed over time, how changes vary across demographic groups, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, and relationships between online and offline retail.

arxiv-2503-18684.title: Efficient Continual Adaptation of Pretrained Robotic Policy with Online Meta-Learned Adapters
arxiv-2503-18684.creator: Ruiqi Zhu, Endong Sun, Guanhe Huang, Oya Celiktutan
arxiv-2503-18684.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ruiqi Zhu, Endong Sun, Guanhe Huang, Oya Celiktutan. Continual adaptation is essential for general autonomous agents. For example, a household robot pretrained with a repertoire of skills must still adapt to unseen tasks specific to each household. Motivated by this, building upon parameter-efficient fine-tuning in language models, prior works have explored lightweight adapters to adapt pretrained policies, which can preserve learned features from the pretraining phase and demonstrate good adaptation performances. However, these approaches treat task learning separately, limiting knowledge transfer between tasks.

arxiv-2505-13614.title: place_keeper
arxiv-2505-13614.description: Abstract The high dimensional parameter space of modern deep neural networks — the neuromanifold — is endowed with a unique metric tensor defined by the Fisher information, estimating which is crucial for both theory and practical methods in deep learning.

arxiv-2602-18097.title: Interacting safely with cyclists using Hamilton-Jacobi reachability and reinforcement learning
arxiv-2602-18097.creator: Aarati Andrea Noronha, Jean Oh This manuscript was completed in 2020 as part of the first author’s graduate thesis at Carnegie Mellon University.
arxiv-2602-18097.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a framework for enabling autonomous vehicles to interact with cyclists in a manner that balances safety and optimality. The approach integrates Hamilton–Jacobi reachability analysis with deep Q-learning to jointly address safety guarantees and time-efficient navigation.

openalex-w4416290809.title: Diagnosis and Management of Heat-related Illness: Clinical and Molecular Perspectives
openalex-w4416290809.creator: Julie Helms, Kenta Kondo, Kunihiko Nagakari, Toshiaki Iba
openalex-w4416290809.description: Heat-related illness (HRI) represents a growing public health challenge in the context of global warming. Ranging from mild symptoms such as heat cramps to life-threatening heatstroke, HRI requires prompt recognition and appropriate management to reduce morbidity and mortality....

pmc-10629767.title: Astrogliosis marker 11C-SL25.1188 PET in traumatic brain injury with persistent symptoms
pmc-10629767.creator: Yuko Koshimori, Michael D Cusimano, Erica L Vieira, Pablo M Rusjan, Stephen J Kish, Neil Vasdev, Sho Moriguchi, Isabelle Boileau, Thomas Chao, Zahra Nasser, M Ishrat Husain, Khunsa Faiz, Joeffre Braga, Jeffrey H Meyer
pmc-10629767.description: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is common but little is known why up to a third of patients have persisting symptoms. Astrogliosis, a pathophysiological response to brain injury, may be a potential therapeutic target, but demonstration of astrogliosis in the brain of humans with TBI and persistent symptoms is lacking.Astroglial marker monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) total distribution volume (11C-SL25.

pmc-11551939.title: Challenges in the Concurrent Management of Severe Mitral Stenosis With LAA Thrombus and Symptomatic Adenomyosis
pmc-11551939.creator: Paras Nazir, Shakir Zada, Moiz Ahmed, Kiran Abbas, Naveedullah Khan, Shueeta Kumari, Ejaz Ul Haq, Muhammad Zeb
pmc-11551939.description: A 49-year-old woman with untreated severe mitral stenosis faced complex management challenges in a resource-limited setting. Initially presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding, her cardiac condition was discovered during a preoperative work-up for a planned hysterectomy. This case emphasizes the necessity for tailored and transdisciplinary management approaches.

pmc-11691325.title: PRESERVING CELL HOMEOSTASIS AS AN AGING MODULTATION STRATEGY
pmc-11691325.creator: Dennis Lox
pmc-11691325.description: The cell desires to maintain homeostasis. The most efficient and productive method to achieve cell homeostasis, is utilization of the Longevity Pathway AMPK-SIRT1. This allows processes to repair, induce positive patterns that lead to systemic efficiency. The Longevity Pathway may be activated by exercise, drugs, MOTS-c (a mitochondrial derived peptide), Irisin (a adipomyokine Sestrin), and circadian clock genes.

pmc-12444528.title: Identification of Tripeptide Inhibitors Targeting MAPK3 in Leishmania martiniquensis and Leishmania orientalis Using Molecular Modeling, Virtual Screening, Molecular Dynamics, and In Vitro Approach
pmc-12444528.creator: Duangnapa Kiriwan, Tatiana F. Vieira, Nutnaree Kumsiri, Sergio F. Sousa, Kiattawee Choowongkomon
pmc-12444528.description: MAPK3 has been identified as a potential drug target due to its role in the Leishmania life cycle. This study focused on two species prevalent in Thailand: Leishmania martiniquensis and Leishmania orientalis. Using an in silico strategies, we screened an in-house library of 8000 tripeptides to identify potential MAPK3 inhibitors.

pmc-12539189.title: Risk-taking behaviors in relation to religiosity and familial support among university students: a latent class analysis
pmc-12539189.creator: Mahsa Tebyanian, Shima Ataee, Abbas Abbasi-Ghahramanloo, Sima Afrashteh, Mohammad Sabaghan, Masoud Imani, Kazem Alizadeh-Barzian, Zahra Movahednia, Nima Daneshi
pmc-12539189.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundHigh-risk behaviors such as substance use, unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, and violence are common among university students and can lead to serious health issues. Research on high-risk behaviors among Iranian university students is limited, with many aspects still unexplored.

pmc-12540228.title: Acute Inflammatory Responses to Blood Flow Restriction Training: A Systematic Review
pmc-12540228.creator: Sarah Barawi, Kevin Happ, Michael Behringer
pmc-12540228.description: BackgroundThe effects of Blood Flow Restriction (BFR) training are well-established, but its impact on the inflammatory response remains unclear. This systematic review evaluates whether BFR training induces acute inflammation by analyzing changes in inflammatory parameters.MethodsThis review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. The literature search was performed across PubMed, Web of Science, BISp-Surf and Google Scholar up to July 2025.

pmc-13096382.title: Comprehensive bioinformatic analysis reveals TRPM4 as a biomarker for pan-cancer progression and macrophage infiltration
pmc-13096382.creator: Xu Huang, Mingyang Hong, Ling Gu, Xingsong Zhang, PanFeng Feng, Ruikun Hu
pmc-13096382.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIon channels play key regulatory roles in cancer pathophysiology. They are also considered promising therapeutic targets. The transient receptor potential melastatin 4 (TRPM4) is a nonselective monovalent cation channel, recently identified as critical in necrosis by sodium overload.

pmc-13212577.title: Focused ultrasound thalamotomy improves voice tremor in essential tremor: objective insight from artificial intelligence
pmc-13212577.creator: Francesca Pistoia, Patrizia Sucapane, Francesco Asci, Gennaro Saporito, Giovanni Costantini, Valerio Cesarini, Giovanni Saggio, Simona Sacco, Antonio Suppa
pmc-13212577.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The impact of Magnetic Resonance Imaging-guided Focused Ultrasound (MRgFUS) on vocal tremor is largely underexplored. We used artificial intelligence to investigate changes in vocal tremor in ET patients undergoing MRgFUS. Eighty-three controls and ET patients (mean age-SEM 70.0–1.0 years), including 39 patients without and 44 patients with clinically overt voice tremor, were assessed before and 24 h after MRgFUS targeting the ventral intermediate nucleus (Vim).

pmc-13234429.title: Distinct finger-tapping feature in progressive supranuclear palsy correlates with motor function and brain atrophy
pmc-13234429.creator: Zijian Chen, Wenwen Xu, Ruonan Duan, Min Tian, Qingchao Yang, Yue Yin, Xiao Tang, Tianrui Wen, Dandan Guo, Yiming Liu
pmc-13234429.description: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a rare neurodegenerative disorder characterized by 4-repeat tau deposition, whose symptoms overlap with Parkinson’s disease (PD). It is necessary to develop objective biomarkers for accurate differentiation. This study used video-based kinematic analysis to assess finger-tapping performance in 31 PSP patients, 31 PD patients, and 30 healthy controls (HC).

pmc-13320188.title: Molecular characterization of emerging bacterial communities associated with honey bees
pmc-13320188.creator: Shazia Amin, Shakir Ullah, Nasreen Nasreen, Ioannis A Giantsis, Maria V Alvanou, Sadaf Niaz, Turki M Dawoud, Esmael M Alyami, Youssouf Ali Younous, Adil Khan
pmc-13320188.description: Honey bees are vital pollinators essential for ecosystems and global agriculture, but their populations are declining due to pressures caused by pests. This study reports the presence of Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus terrae, and Pseudomonas spp. in four different honey bee species in Pakistan for the first time, uncovering a previously neglected aspect of honey bee microbiology.

pmc-13424134.title: TGF-β and IL-2 differentially shape T follicular regulatory cell differentiation and stability in vitro
pmc-13424134.creator: Luisa Bach, Yinshui Chang, Olin Arteaga Transito, Mohammadamin Ghasemi, Lisa Maria Steinheuer, Teresa Steffen, Elena De Domenico, Thomas Ulas, F Thomas Wunderlich, Marc D Beyer, Kevin Thurley, Dirk Baumjohann
pmc-13424134.description: T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and T follicular regulatory (Tfr) cells play critical roles in regulating the activity of the germinal center (GC), which is essential for the generation of high-affinity antibodies. In the GC, Tfh cells help B cells to proliferate and to differentiate into memory B cells and long-lived plasma cells.

pmc-13588250.title: Scopolamine Prevents Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Depressive Disorder, Potentially via Its Anti-Inflammatory Effects
pmc-13588250.creator: Yunxiao Zhang, Hao Fu, Wanpu Yan, Shuo Li, Jiheng Chen
pmc-13588250.description: BackgroundDepression imposes a heavy global disease burden accompanied by mitochondrial injury and neuroinflammation predominantly in the prefrontal cortex. Using a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) rat model, this study aimed to explore the impacts of scopolamine on brain mitochondrial function and its underlying mechanisms.MethodsTwelve male Wistar rats aged 6–8 weeks were randomly assigned to three groups: control, CUMS, and CUMS+scopolamine.
